name: Centrism
summary: Centrism is a position between left and right that favours moderate, gradual and pragmatic reform. Its best-documented strands are Third Way and radical centrism, which accept market economies while keeping a liberal welfare state, and stress opportunity with responsibility. It has no fixed program, so many policy answers are inferences.
scope: Mainstream Western centrism as documented in Third Way politics (Giddens, Blair, Clinton, Schroeder) and radical centrism (Satin, Halstead and Lind, Avlon). Excludes parties merely labelled centrist, centrist populism and agrarian or Christian-democratic variants. As a positional label rather than a program, many answers are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Centrists support a liberal welfare state; universal coverage is inferred as a common but not defining centrist position.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Moderates accept some wage floors but split on a substantial rise; inferred from balanced economic stance.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Radical centrists favour market-based solutions with strong oversight in the public interest, so neither side is taken outright.

public-ownership.rationale: Third Way centrism accepts competitive markets and public-private partnerships rather than broad nationalisation.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Third Way figures cut some taxes to attract investment, while other centrists accept moderate redistribution; adherents are split.

unions-good.rationale: Clinton praised firms sharing gains with workers but centrists have no fixed union line; inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Centrism sits close to liberalism, which values property; inferred, not stressed.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Strong oversight is favoured alongside market solutions, so tighter regulation is a case-by-case question.

cut-welfare.rationale: Third Way reform favours workfare and a hand-up rather than cutting welfare outright.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not a centrist goal; inferred from acceptance of conventional market enterprise.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; moderates are split between security and liberty.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed as a core issue; centrist opinion is divided.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; centrists are divided between liberal speech norms and social-harm concerns.

strong-leader.rationale: Radical centrists want grounded movements and institutional reform rather than a single charismatic leader.

state-harmful.rationale: Centrists support a liberal welfare state and institutional reform, and reject abolishing the state.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from mainstream centre-left Third Way politicians such as Clinton; contested among centrists.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed; centrists are split on this.

decide-locally.rationale: No fixed centrist position on decentralisation; inferred.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from moderate, evidence-oriented reform attitudes.

traditional-family.rationale: Clinton stressed family and parental responsibility, yet social liberal centrists are less traditional; split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Social liberalism is a main centrist variant, so legalisation is inferred as the mainstream view.

abortion-legal.rationale: Social liberal centrism leans pro-choice in most cases; inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Inferred from liberal-leaning centrism favouring secular public institutions, though Christian democrats differ.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Social liberal centrism generally supports measures against discrimination; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Not addressed; moderates are split between cosmopolitan and traditional views.

gradual-change.rationale: Centrists favour gradual change and prioritise prudence in institutional reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; centrist parties are split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: European centrist parties supported integration and the EU; inferred more broadly.

free-trade.rationale: The Third Way accepts global economic integration and works to attract investment within it.

nation-first.rationale: Radical centrists support global engagement; inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Third Way leaders such as Clinton and Blair supported intervention; inferred for the mainstream.

open-borders.rationale: Moderate centrists do not advocate abolishing borders; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Third Way centrism prizes growth and the revenue it generates.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Environmental protection is a Third Way theme but drastic action is not defining; split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Radical centrism is pragmatic and not techno-utopian; inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: Centrists favour gradual, prudent reform over revolutionary change.

experts-over-public.rationale: Evidence-based policy appeals to centrists, but they also want democratic legitimacy; split.

central-planning.rationale: Third Way accepts competitive markets as the main engine of wealth.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred from acceptance of conventional markets with public-private partnerships.

land-value-tax.rationale: A single-tax system is not a centrist position; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Third Way stresses work and responsibility rather than unconditional payments, though some radical centrists back it.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Third Way accepts globalisation and free trade; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Markets are the main engine of wealth, with state action where markets fail.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Centrism has no documented position on this; adherents are divided, so it is answered neutrally.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Centrism rejects abolishing the market economy.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Centrism accepts conventional institutions and fiscal discipline; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Third Way relies on markets, not state-run wage and price bargaining; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Centrism operates within plural party democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; centrists in monarchies accept it, others do not.

democracy-best.rationale: Clinton's New Covenant stresses democratic community and citizen involvement; centrism is rooted in plural democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Centrists favour institutional reform within representative systems; inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not a centrist position; inferred from its moderate, pragmatic and liberal-democratic outlook.

political-violence-never.rationale: Inferred from the moderate, prudential, gradualist outlook.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred from liberal-leaning centrism, though Christian democrats differ.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Not centrist; inferred from liberal pluralism.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Centrism supports a liberal welfare state and public institutions.

military-superiority.rationale: Centrism has no documented position on this; adherents are divided, so it is answered neutrally.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Clinton frames the country as one community going up or down together, rejecting class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Third Way stresses equality of opportunity paired with personal responsibility.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Centrism has no documented position on this; adherents are divided, so it is answered neutrally.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Centrism has no documented position on this; adherents are divided, so it is answered neutrally.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not a centrist position; inferred from its moderate, pragmatic and liberal-democratic outlook.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Opportunity with responsibility and community suggests neither pure self-interest nor self-denial.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rights with responsibilities pairs them rather than ranking duties first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental protection is a theme but the philosophical question is not addressed.

limit-population.rationale: Centrism has no documented position on this; adherents are divided, so it is answered neutrally.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Third Way accepts growth and globalisation; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Centrism has no documented position on this; adherents are divided, so it is answered neutrally.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from prudence and democratic accountability.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Centrism has no documented position on this; adherents are divided, so it is answered neutrally.

restore-past-order.rationale: Centrists favour prudent reform, not restoring a lost order; inferred.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Radical centrists reject ideology and left-right labels, favouring realism and pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: Centrists work within elections and parties; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: Centrism has no documented position on this; adherents are divided, so it is answered neutrally.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not a centrist position; inferred from its moderate, pragmatic and liberal-democratic outlook.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not a centrist position; inferred from its moderate, pragmatic and liberal-democratic outlook.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Third Way relies on markets and opportunity, not distribution by need.

production-for-use.rationale: Third Way accepts markets and competition as the engine of wealth.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Third Way accepts markets and private enterprise rather than seeing profit as exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Alien to centrism, which rejects class rule.

collective-farming.rationale: Not a centrist position; inferred from its moderate, pragmatic and liberal-democratic outlook.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Third Way accepts capitalism and globalisation; inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: Centrists support a liberal welfare state funded by taxes.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred from commitment to democratic participation.

state-as-business.rationale: Public-private partnerships are favoured but citizens-as-customers is not a stated centrist idea.

positive-liberty.rationale: Third Way and social liberalism link freedom with opportunity and social capital.

national-rebirth.rationale: Radical centrists reject mass emotional radicalism in favour of realism; inferred.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not a centrist position; inferred from its moderate, pragmatic and liberal-democratic outlook.

universal-morality.rationale: Centrism has no documented position on this; adherents are divided, so it is answered neutrally.

single-common-good.rationale: Centrists blend ideas from left and right and balance interests; inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Centrism has no documented position on this; adherents are divided, so it is answered neutrally.

revive-national-language.rationale: Centrism has no documented position on this; adherents are divided, so it is answered neutrally.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not a Third Way aim; inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Clinton stressed a balanced budget and criticised structural deficits; Third Way favours fiscal discipline.

force-without-un.rationale: Centrism has no documented position on this; adherents are divided, so it is answered neutrally.

notes: Strands differ: Christian-democratic and centre-right variants lean more conservative, centre-left Third Way variants more social-democratic. Centrism is a positional label, so most answers are inferences.
